recommendation: Keep the audit commit. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-11061 unless the work group makes a new decision about current Consent.grantor/Consent.grantee cardinalities or invariants.
issue_request: FHIR-11061 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for DSTU2 Consent. It requested changing Consent.consentor to Consent.consentingParty and defining that party as either the grantor responsible for granting rights in a Consent Directive or the grantee responsible for complying with the directive.
initial_application: Git commit 687d10304fe8c9e42f5ff4e7ff3c322653b167f4 explicitly listed GF#11061 and changed the Consent spreadsheet source from Consent.consentor to Consent.consentingParty with the approved grantor-or-grantee definition.
additional_context: Later Consent modeling moved from Consent.consentingParty to Consent.performer and then, through FHIR-31906, to separate Consent.grantor and Consent.grantee elements. FHIR-27779 later clarified that a Consent without listed grantor or grantee may be a subject preference statement and is not in force. FHIR-31906 and FHIR-27779 are already represented on the combined branch by their own reconciliation commits.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build-scope Consent source in source/fhir.ini and source/consent/structuredefinition-Consent.xml already conveys the approved semantics; reintroducing Consent.consentingParty or adding a new constraint would conflict with later approved modeling.

related_jiras.note: Converted Consent.performer into current Consent.grantor and Consent.grantee elements with usage-note guidance for fully computable consent actors.
Clarified that a Consent without listed performer, now interpreted as without listed grantor or grantee, may be a subject preference statement and is not in force.
Earlier Consent.performer clarification highlighted grantor/grantee ambiguity before the later split.
Later correction confirms the current grantor and grantee definitions used in Consent.
